options.name: client_override_options
options.description: Client override options (developer use). For example, can be used to override the DigitalOcean API endpoint for an internal test suite. If provided, these options will knock out existing options.

options.name: disable_lets_encrypt_dns_records
options.description:
A boolean value indicating whether to disable automatic DNS record creation for
Let's Encrypt certificates that are added to the load balancer.

options.name: droplet_ids
options.description: An array containing the IDs of the Droplets assigned to the load balancer.

options.name: enable_backend_keepalive
options.description:
A boolean value indicating whether HTTP keepalive connections are maintained to target
Droplets.

options.name: enable_proxy_protocol
options.description: A boolean value indicating whether PROXY Protocol is in use.

options.name: firewall
options.description: An object specifying allow and deny rules to control traffic to the load balancer.

options.name: forwarding_rules
options.description: An array of objects specifying the forwarding rules for a load balancer.

options.name: health_checks
options.description: An object specifying health check settings for the load balancer.

options.name: http_idle_timeout_seconds
options.description: An integer value which configures the idle timeout for HTTP requests to the target droplets.

options.name: module_override_options
options.description: Module override options (developer use). Can be used to override module options to support experimental or future options. If provided, these options will knock out existing options.

options.name: name
options.description: A human-readable name for a load balancer instance.

options.name: project_id
options.description:
The ID of the project that the load balancer is associated with. If no ID is provided at creation, the load balancer associates with the user's default
project.
 If an invalid project ID is provided, the load balancer will not be created.

options.name: redirect_http_to_https
options.description:
A boolean value indicating whether HTTP requests to the load balancer on port 80 will
be redirected to HTTPS on port 443.

options.name: region
options.description: The slug identifier for the region where the resource will initially be available.

options.name: size
options.description:
Deprecated. This field has been replaced by the size_unit field for all regions except in AMS2, NYC2,
and SFO1.
 Each available load balancer size now equates to the load balancer having a set number of nodes. C(lb-small) = 1 node, C(lb-medium) = 3 nodes, C(lb-large) = 6 nodes.

options.name: size_unit
options.description:
How many nodes the load balancer contains. Each additional node increases the load balancer's ability to manage more connections. Load balancers can be scaled up or down, and you can change the number of nodes after creation up to once
per hour.
 This field is currently not available in the AMS2, NYC2, or SFO1 regions. Use the size field to scale load balancers that reside in these regions.

options.name: state
options.description: State of the resource, C(present) to create, C(absent) to destroy.

options.name: sticky_sessions
options.description: An object specifying sticky sessions settings for the load balancer.

options.name: timeout
options.description: Polling timeout in seconds.

options.name: token
options.description: DigitalOcean API token. There are several environment variables which can be used to provide this value. C(DIGITALOCEAN_ACCESS_TOKEN), C(DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN), C(DO_API_TOKEN), C(DO_API_KEY), C(DO_OAUTH_TOKEN) and C(OAUTH_TOKEN)

options.name: vpc_uuid
options.description: A string specifying the UUID of the VPC to which the load balancer is assigned.
